tagline: Old Town’s river history meets the road toward US 278.
intro: At Old Town Bluffton’s northern edge, SC 46 turns from May River Road onto Bluffton Road and runs northeast toward US 278. South Carolina’s 2012 act repealed the 1978 Beaufort County scenic-highway act and established the May River Scenic Byway on specified portions of SC 46, S-66 and S-13.

Old Town grew on a bluff beside the May River. Visit Bluffton says the street layout suggests a summer settlement that developed into a commercial center supplied from Savannah by river. From Boundary Street, the southern continuation of Bluffton Road, the northbound SC 46 drive reaches the Bluffton Parkway traffic circle and then US 278.

moments.title: Campbell Chapel
moments.text: At 23 Boundary Street, Campbell Chapel began in 1853 as a church built by a white congregation. An African Methodist Episcopal congregation acquired it in 1874. Its 2019 National Register listing recognized Greek Revival architecture and the survival of much of its nineteenth-century fabric.

moments.title: May River Road junction
moments.text: SC 46 turns north from May River Road onto Bluffton Road at the edge of the historic center. The street continues south as Boundary Street, a former SC 46 segment; May River Road continues east as Bruin Road.

moments.title: Bluffton Parkway circle
moments.text: On its northeastward course along Bluffton Road, SC 46 reaches a traffic circle with Bluffton Parkway. The state highway ends farther along at US 278, opposite The Crescent.
